props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who buys a lulav from his fellow in the Sabbatical year -- [the seller] gives him the etrog as a gift, because one may not buy it in the Sabbatical year
Rav Huna: if [the seller] will not give it as a gift, [the buyer] folds the etrog's price into the lulav's
because one does not hand the money of Sabbatical produce to an am ha'aretz
the baraita: one does not hand an am ha'aretz Sabbatical-produce money beyond the food of three meals
the baraita: and if he did hand it over, he says 'let these coins be deconsecrated onto produce I have in my house', and eats that produce in Sabbatical sanctity
the baraita: where was this [three-meal allowance] said? -- of one who buys from ownerless produce
the baraita: but buying from guarded produce, even half an issar's worth is forbidden

the mishna (Sheviit 9:1): rue, amaranth, shitim, purslane, mountain coriander, river celery and field rocket are exempt from tithes and may be bought from anyone in the Sabbatical year, for nothing like them is guarded
Rav Sheshet: they taught [the pigam mishna] of an amount of man (sustenance) -- the three-meal limit is not breached
the stam: 'man' means sustenance, as written 'and the king appointed (vayman) for them' (Daniel 1:5)
the stam: the mishna's lulav is a sixth-year lulav entering the seventh
the stam: for an etrog we go by its picking
the stam's reading of the Bikkurim mishna: both Rabban Gamliel and R' Eliezer go by the etrog's ripening for the Sabbatical year
Rabban Gamliel (Bikkurim 2:6): the etrog is like a tree in three ways -- orla, fourth-year fruit and the Sabbatical year -- and like a vegetable in one: it is tithed at the time of its picking
R' Eliezer: the etrog is like a tree in every respect [including tithes]
the stam: the mishna's tanna holds like this tanna [the Usha decision]
R' Yosei: Avtolemos testified in the name of five elders: the etrog goes by its picking for tithes
the restored text of the five elders' testimony: ... and by its ripening for the Sabbatical year
our masters were counted at Usha and said: the etrog goes by its picking, for tithes and for the Sabbatical year alike
the stam: who mentioned the Sabbatical year? -- the baraita is lacking a clause, and teaches thus
the stam: the reason is that it is a sixth-year lulav -- implying a seventh-year lulav is holy [with Sabbatical sanctity]
reed and vine leaves piled in a heap on the field: gathered for eating, they have Sabbatical sanctity
gathered for wood, they have no Sabbatical sanctity
the stam: there it is different, for the verse says 'for you, for food' (Vayikra 25:6)
'for you' is like 'for food': [Sabbatical sanctity holds of] that whose benefit and whose consumption coincide
wood is excluded, whose benefit comes after its consumption
Rava: wood unspecified stands for fuel
the stam: [whether] wood for fuel [has sanctity] is a tannaitic dispute
the first tanna: one does not hand over Sabbatical produce for soaking [flax] or for laundering
R' Yosei: one may hand it over
the first tanna's reason: the verse says 'for food' -- not for soaking and not for laundering
R' Yosei's reason: the verse says 'for you' -- for all your needs, even soaking and laundering
for the first tanna, that 'for you' is like 'for food' -- soaking and laundering are excluded, whose benefit comes after consumption
for R' Yosei, 'for food' is needed to exclude a poultice (remedy)
the baraita: 'for food' -- and not for a poultice
the baraita's rival reading: or perhaps 'for food' -- and not for laundering?
the baraita: I include laundering, which is alike for every person, and exclude a poultice, which is not alike for every person
the baraita: 'for food' -- not for a poultice, not for sprinkling, not to make an emetic of it
the stam: that baraita is R' Yosei's
(entertained) were the baraita the Rabbis' [the first tanna's]
(inside the hypothesis) it would also list soaking and laundering -- which it does not
R' Elazar: Sabbatical produce is deconsecrated only by way of purchase
R' Yochanan: both by way of purchase and by way of redemption
the stam: R' Yochanan needs 'and if you sell' for R' Yosei bar Chanina's teaching

R' Yosei bar Chanina: come and see how severe the dust of the Sabbatical year is -- one who trades in Sabbatical produce ends by selling his movables and his vessels, as it says 'in this year of Jubilee you shall return' (Vayikra 25:13) and next to it 'and if you sell' (25:14)
the stam: R' Elazar needs 'for it is a Jubilee, it is holy' for the baraita's teaching [that Sabbatical produce seizes its price]
the baraita: 'for it is a Jubilee, it is holy' -- as the holy seizes its price, so Sabbatical produce seizes its price
the baraita: Sabbatical produce seizes its price -- as the holy seizes its price and is forbidden, so Sabbatical produce seizes its price and is [still] forbidden
the baraita: Scripture says 'it shall be' -- it remains in its state [and does not go out to profane status]
(entertained by the baraita) as the holy seizes its price and goes out to profane status, so Sabbatical produce would go out to profane status?

the baraita: how so? one bought meat with Sabbatical produce -- both must be removed in the Sabbatical year; bought fish with the meat -- the meat goes out and the fish comes in; wine with the fish, oil with the wine, likewise
the baraita: the last [bought] each time enters [Sabbatical status], and the fruit itself stays forbidden
the stam: since it says 'bought ... bought', by purchase -- yes; by redemption -- no
R' Meir: Sabbatical produce and second tithe alike are deconsecrated onto cattle, beasts and fowl, alive or slaughtered
the Sages: onto slaughtered ones they are deconsecrated, onto live ones they are not
the Sages' ground: a decree, lest he raise herds from them
Rava: the dispute is over males; over females all agree -- onto slaughtered yes, onto live no, lest he raise herds from them
Rav Ashi (first version): the dispute [R' Elazar vs R' Yochanan] is over the original produce
Rav Ashi (first version): over the second produce all agree -- by purchase or by redemption
the baraita: one with a Sabbatical sela who wants to buy a shirt goes to his usual shopkeeper, buys produce with the sela, gives him the produce as a gift, and receives the sela back as a gift
Rav Ashi (second version): the dispute is over the second produce
Rav Ashi (second version): over the original produce all agree -- by purchase yes, by redemption no
Rav Ashi: the 'Sabbatical produce' of the R' Yochanan baraita means Sabbatical MONEY
(entertained) otherwise, the baraita's 'second tithe' would be the tithe itself
but it is written 'and you shall bind up the money in your hand' (Devarim 14:25) -- the tithe itself is redeemed onto money
rather it is tithe money -- and here too, Sabbatical money

schemas.gloss_en: מאי טעמיה דרבי אלעזר? דכתיב בשנת היובל הזאת (Vayikra 25:13) וסמיך ליה וכי תמכרו ממכר (25:14) -- דרך מקח ולא דרך חילול (the reason as the stam gives it)
ורבי יוחנן מאי טעמיה? דכתיב כי יובל היא קדש (Vayikra 25:12) -- מה קדש בין דרך מקח בין דרך חילול, אף שביעית בין דרך מקח בין דרך חילול (the reason as the stam gives it)
שנאמר בשנת היובל הזאת תשובו איש אל אחוזתו, וסמיך ליה וכי תמכרו ממכר לעמיתך -- the trader in Sabbatical produce ends by selling his possessions
כי יובל היא קדש -- מה קדש תופס את דמיו אף שביעית תופסת את דמיה
מה קדש תופס את דמיו ואסור, אף שביעית תופסת את דמיה ואסורה
אי, מה קדש תופס דמיו ויוצא לחולין, אף שביעית תופסת את דמיה ויוצאת לחולין?

grounds.gloss_en: תלמוד לומר תהיה -- בהוייתה תהא: the produce stays in its state (= p_bk_behavayata)

supports.gloss_en: דתניא: אין מוסרין דמי פירות שביעית לעם הארץ יותר ממזון שלש סעודות
מאי משמע דהאי מן לישנא דמזוני הוא -- דכתיב וימן להם המלך (no support kind names a lexical proof; svara is the nearest)
דתניא: ... ורבותינו נמנו באושא ואמרו ... בין למעשר בין לשביעית
טעמא דלולב בר שישית הנכנס לשביעית הוא, הא דשביעית קדוש -- inferred from the stam's own okimta (marker טעמא ד... הא; dika_nami is the nearest kind)
דתניא: אין מוסרין פירות שביעית לא למשרה ולא לכבוסה; רבי יוסי אומר מוסרין
דתניא, אמר רבי יוסי בר חנינא: בוא וראה כמה קשה אבקה של שביעית
כדתניא: כי יובל היא קדש -- מה קדש תופס את דמיו אף שביעית תופסת את דמיה
תניא כוותיה דרבי אלעזר: ... לקח בפירות שביעית בשר ... לקח בבשר דגים ...; מדקתני לקח לקח, אלמא דרך מקח אין דרך חילול לא (40b.10, = p_diyuk_lakach)

deflected_by.gloss_en: והא דקתני לקח לקח -- איידי דתנא רישא לקח, תנא נמי סיפא לקח: the wording is stylistic, so it proves nothing (part of Rav Ashi's first version)

refuted_by.gloss_en: Ravina's objection fells the first version (second produce does need purchase), and Rav Ashi withdraws it (אלא, 41a.4); the איידי reading goes with it -- the nearest life-cycle state to a retraction

supports.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דרבי יוחנן: אחד שביעית ואחד מעשר שני מתחללין על בהמה חיה ועוף ... (the baraita's מתחללין)
והא כתיב וצרת הכסף בידך -- the tithe itself is redeemed onto money, not animals; so the baraita's 'tithe' is tithe money
אלא דמי מעשר -- הכא נמי דמי שביעית

alternatives.gloss_en: the survivor: not for a poultice

objections.gloss_en: וליתיב ליה בהדיא? -- why the artifice; let him pay for the etrog openly

answered_by.gloss_en: לפי שאין מוסרין דמי פירות שביעית לעם הארץ (= p_ein_mosrin)

objections.gloss_en: מתיב רב ששת: ומן המופקר שלש סעודות ותו לא? ורמינהו: ... ניקחין מכל אדם בשביעית -- the pigam herbs, which are not guarded, may be bought from anyone, with no stated limit

answered_by.gloss_en: הוא מותיב לה והוא מפרק לה: בכדי מן שנו (= p_bichdei_man; likewise R' Yochanan via Rabbah bar bar Chana)

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי, לולב נמי! -- if Sabbatical money may not be handed to him, the lulav too [should not be bought]

answered_by.gloss_en: לולב בר שישית הנכנס לשביעית הוא (= p_lulav_bar_shishit)

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי, אתרוג נמי -- בת שישית הנכנסת לשביעית היא! -- then the etrog too would be a sixth-year fruit
והא בין רבן גמליאל ובין רבי אליעזר לענין שביעית אתרוג בתר חנטה אזלינן! דתנן: אתרוג שוה לאילן בשלשה דרכים ... לערלה ולרבעי ולשביעית

answered_by.gloss_en: הוא דאמר כי האי תנא -- the mishna's tanna holds like the Usha decision (= p_matnitin_keusha)

objections.gloss_en: שביעית מאן דכר שמיה? -- the Usha clause's 'and for shviit' presupposes a mention of shviit the baraita does not make

answered_by.gloss_en: חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני: אתרוג אחר לקיטה למעשר ואחר חנטה לשביעית (= p_chasurei_mechasra, p_avtolemos_chanata_shviit)

objections.gloss_en: אמאי? עצים בעלמא הוא, ועצים אין בהן משום קדושת שביעית -- (דתנן) leaves gathered for wood have no Sabbatical sanctity

answered_by.gloss_en: שאני התם, דאמר קרא לכם לאכלה ... יצאו עצים שהנאתן אחר ביעורן -- wood for burning is excluded; [a lulav is not burnt] (der_stam_lachem_leochla)

objections.gloss_en: והאיכא עצים דמשחן, דהנאתן וביעורן שוה! -- there is wood whose benefit and consumption coincide

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר רבא: סתם עצים להסקה הן עומדין (= p_rava_stam_etzim)

objections.gloss_en: ותנא קמא, הא כתיב לכם! -- 'for you' (all your needs) is written

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא לכם דומיא דלאכלה: מי שהנאתו וביעורו שוה, יצאו משרה וכבוסה שהנאתן אחר ביעורן (= p_tk_yatzu_mishra, attributed to the first tanna)

objections.gloss_en: ורבי יוסי, הא כתיב לאכלה! -- 'for food' is written

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא מיבעי ליה לאכלה ולא למלוגמא, כדתניא (= p_ryosei_lo_lemelugma)

objections.gloss_en: מה ראית לרבות את הכבוסה ולהוציא את המלוגמא? -- why include laundering and exclude a poultice, rather than the reverse?

answered_by.gloss_en: מרבה אני את הכבוסה ששוה בכל אדם, ומוציא את המלוגמא שאינה שוה לכל אדם (= p_kvisa_shava_lechol_adam)

objections.gloss_en: ורבי יוחנן, האי כי תמכרו ממכר מאי עביד ליה? -- what does R' Yochanan do with R' Elazar's juxtaposition?

answered_by.gloss_en: מיבעי ליה לכדרבי יוסי בר חנינא (= p_ryochanan_mivaei_rybc)

objections.gloss_en: ורבי אלעזר, האי קרא דרבי יוחנן מאי עביד ליה? -- what does R' Elazar do with כי יובל היא קדש?

answered_by.gloss_en: מיבעי ליה לכדתניא: מה קדש תופס את דמיו אף שביעית תופסת את דמיה (= p_relazar_mivaei_tofeset)

objections.gloss_en: איתיביה רבינא לרב אשי: the sela baraita -- והא הכא דפרי שני הוא, וקתני דרך מקח אין דרך חילול לא! -- second produce, yet only purchase works
